# Join The Lab

Kabir Lab welcomes Savannah State students interested in computational chemistry, molecular modeling, scientific programming, and data analysis.

## Who Should Consider Applying

Students who are curious about molecular science, willing to document their work carefully, and interested in learning computational tools are encouraged to prepare a structured inquiry.

## Example Project Types

- Literature-guided computational chemistry projects.
- Molecular modeling and visualization.
- Python or shell workflow development.
- Publication-data and repository curation.
- Simulation analysis and reproducibility checks.

## Skills Students Can Learn

- Linux command-line work.
- Python scripting for scientific data.
- Molecular visualization and structure preparation.
- Electronic-structure and molecular-simulation concepts.
- Research notebooks, version control, and scientific communication.

## Application Materials

Prepare one concise email or form response with:

1. Name, major, and year.
2. Short statement of research interest.
3. Relevant chemistry, mathematics, programming, or physics courses.
4. Weekly availability.
5. CV or resume.

::: {.warning-note}
Weekly hours, minimum semester commitment, position type, transcript requirements, and application destination will be posted after the lab confirms current openings.
:::

## Research Expectations

Students are expected to keep careful records, communicate progress regularly, respect data integrity, and distinguish tested results from hypotheses or exploratory notes.
